draft.title: Factors affecting justice in civil cases
card: The Victorian Study Design judges the civil system against three principles of justice: fairness, equality and access. Costs and time can each help or harm all three.

a party may pay lawyers, court fees and expert witnesses. High costs can stop people starting a case or force them to settle, which harms access. A party who can afford better lawyers may also have an advantage, which harms equality.

a case can take months or years to reach a hearing. Long delays add to costs, wear down parties and make evidence harder to gather, which harms fairness. Parties may give up or accept a poor settlement.
A civil case with lower costs and quicker steps gives parties a better chance of a fair outcome. The system works to reduce both, but they can still limit justice.
draft.remember: High costs and long delays can shut people out of court or push them into weak settlements.

a.q: Why can high legal costs reduce access to justice in a civil dispute?
opts: Some people cannot afford to start or continue a case
Courts refuse to hear cases from people with low incomes
Judges give more weight to the party who spent more
Costs make every civil case last longer than a year
a.why: Access means being able to use the system. If people cannot pay for lawyers and fees, they may not start a case or may give up. Courts do not refuse people because of income, so the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about whether a person can get into the system at all.

b.q: Priya sues a builder over faulty work. Her case is delayed for two years. By then her main witness has moved away and she has spent most of her savings. She accepts a low settlement. Which factor most directly affected fairness here?
opts: Delay, which weakened her evidence and drained her funds
The jury, which decided the facts against her
The remedy, which was an injunction she did not want
The hierarchy, which sent her case to the wrong court
b.why: The long delay made evidence harder to gather and added to her costs, so she settled for less than she may have deserved. The other options are not described in the scenario: no jury, remedy or court error is mentioned.
b.clue: Look for what changed over the two years.

a.best: Some people cannot afford to start or continue a case

b.best: Delay, which weakened her evidence and drained her funds

The three wrong options name things absent from the scenario (an injunction, a wrong court, a jury). Only the delay option matches the scenario's details, so a student can pick it by matching words without understanding fairness. This is very easy for Year 12.

proposal.title: Factors affecting justice in civil cases
card: The civil system is judged against three principles of justice. Fairness is a fair process and hearing, equality is a level footing for all parties, and access is being able to use the system.

a party may pay lawyers, court fees and expert witnesses. High costs can stop people starting a case or push them to settle, which harms access. A party who can afford better lawyers may gain an advantage, which harms equality.

a case can take months or years to reach a hearing. Long delays add to costs, wear down parties and make evidence harder to gather, which harms fairness. Parties may give up or accept a poor settlement.
Lower costs and quicker steps give parties a better chance of a fair outcome. The system works to reduce both, but they can still limit justice.
proposal.remember: High costs and long delays can shut people out of court or push them into weak settlements.

a.q: Why can high legal costs reduce access to justice in a civil dispute?
opts: Some people cannot afford to start or continue a case
Courts refuse to hear cases from people with low incomes
Judges give more weight to the party who spent more
Costs make every civil case last longer than a year
a.why: Access means being able to use the system. If people cannot pay for lawyers and fees, they may not start a case or may give up. Courts do not turn people away because of their income, so the option about courts refusing low-income people is wrong.
a.clue: Think about whether a person can get into the system at all.

b.q: Priya sues a builder over faulty work. The case takes two years to reach a hearing. By then her main witness has moved overseas, and she accepts a low settlement. Which principle did the delay most directly harm, and why?
opts: Fairness, as her witness was gone before the hearing
Access, as she was never able to file her claim
Equality, as the delay was longer than the law allows
Fairness, as the law does not let civil cases settle
b.why: Delay made her evidence harder to gather, so she could not fully present her case. That harms a fair hearing, which is fairness. Access is wrong because Priya did start her case, and settling a civil case is allowed.
b.clue: What did the two years do to her evidence?

a.best: Some people cannot afford to start or continue a case

b.best: Fairness, as her witness was gone before the hearing
